sentences.text: Citrobacter is a genus of Gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, non-spore-forming rods belonging to the family Enterobacteriaceae.
A review reports that Citrobacter species are widely distributed in soil, water and sewage, and are also part of the intestinal flora of humans and animals.
A review reports that Citrobacter species are associated with a range of infections, including urinary tract infections, gastrointestinal diseases, neonatal meningitis and sepsis.
Another review describes Citrobacter strains spreading from carriers or other hospital sources and causing nosocomial infections in hospital settings.
That review also describes the recent emergence and spread of resistance to beta-lactams, carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides and colistin in Citrobacter species.
